reviews.title: great gadget that isn't necessary 😂
reviews.comment: Not an essential purchase, but it's beautiful. Besides having brighter LEDs than the previous version, the mouse glides beautifully. Overpriced? Definitely, but Razer makes a "gaming lifestyle product," so if you have other Razer products, this will be a great match.

reviews.title: Nice, solid pad for the Razer ecosystem!
reviews.comment: Smooth surface, my Razer Basilisk v3 glides over this thing! Pretty RGB effects too. A little pricey, but good value of you can get one on sale. Fits well on any desk. Thin enough not to be intrusive, too.
reviews.author: J. Lowery

reviews.title: Solid function with awesome aesthetics: a high quality product.
reviews.comment:
I gotta say I really do love this thing, but mainly for one big reason: the cable catch. It's simple but is very intuitively placed and quite incredible for a wired mouse. It really improves the feeling of a wired mouse. The surface of the mouse pad is quite nice. It's very smooth and my mouse glides across it. There are also no sharp feeling edges where the surface and LEDs meet, and it is kind on your wrist. Because the back of the mousepad has that rubber grippy material uniformly across it, it sits down perfectly flat on a desk and will not move easily with regular use. If you have sweaty hands you probably will not like the feeling of the mousepad for longer gaming sessions, but it is extremely easy to clean. The RGB on this is definitely the best I've seen on a mousepad. It has the most lighting zones and gets very bright. I run mine at around 50% brightness so it's not distracting when playing in the dark.
Overall the mousepad really just screams quality. The packaging is very nice, the unboxing experience is nice and easy. The braided cable feels extremely nice and fits snugly in USB ports. Even the cable management rubber tie thing feels nice. The mousepad surface feels good and is nice for both regular use and gaming. The LED lighting is, in my opinion, best in class and none of the other big manufacturers really come close. If I had to give it a con, I would say that the software isn't the best and it really is a bit daunting to use at times, but it's not really a big deal if you're using the lighting presets anyways. For $50 it is a pricy mousepad, but it really does feel like you are getting your money's worth out of it.
reviews.author: RedAsh

reviews.title: Best RGB Mouspad I have found on the internet
reviews.comment:
Right off the rip I can say I have scoured the internet and can't find a single mouse pad with RBG lights like these. Every mouse pad I've seen that is RGB simply changes the entire bar of light. This mousepad has multiple nodes of light inside allowing for a beautiful stream of rainbows or whatever color combinations you can imagine. The Razer Synapse program as well as the Chroma Studio are great. Chroma Studio works almost like photoshop allowing for insane levels of customization.
The quality of the mouse pad is great, I like that it's a hard surface personally. One complaint I have is that the pad tends to slide across the desk sometimes when I'm playing games. It needs to be readjusted often so the non-slip backing could have been executed better. It has a nice clip for your mouse wire to rest in allowing you to keep the wiring a bit more managed.
Overall, great mouse pad with probably the best RGB lighting you'll ever find online. IF anyone has found something of equal of better quality I'd love to know about them!
